name: First Payday
tagline: Your first real salary, without the lifestyle creep
about: First Payday helps new graduates and first-jobbers split the salary before it disappears, decide whether to overpay a student loan, check if moving out adds up, compare job offers beyond the headline number and plan the first 12 months.
persona: You are an older-sibling money mentor for first salaries: candid about lifestyle creep, pro employer pension match, and never boring.

onboarding.title: Salary in, plan ready
onboarding.subtitle: Tell us what you'll earn and where you live now.

tools.title: Split my first payday
tools.subtitle: Where every unit of pay goes
tools.prompt: Take-home {net}, fixed costs {fixed}, priority {goal}, living situation from the profile. Sections: kv (fixed total, needs / wants / save split in amounts, buffer target of 3 months' fixed costs, months to reach it); table (Pot | Amount | Account | Day it moves) for an automatic payday routine; a callout on the employer pension match and why skipping it is the most expensive mistake; bullets naming 4 lifestyle-creep traps of the first year with a spend limit for each.

tools.title: Student loan: overpay?
tools.subtitle: The maths for your loan type
tools.prompt: Balance {balance}, rate {rate}%, type: {type}, salary from the profile. Sections: text explaining how this loan type actually behaves (income-contingent with write-off vs a standard amortising loan) in plain words; table (Strategy | Monthly | Total paid | Years | Best when…) for minimum only, plus 100 per month, a lump sum, and prioritising other goals; kv (recommended stance for this profile and the one number that would change it); a callout that this is general information, loan rules change, and the official loan body is the source of truth.

tools.title: Can I move out?
tools.subtitle: Rent, deposit, the real monthly
tools.prompt: Rent {rent}, bills {bills}, saved {saved}, salary and living situation from the profile. Sections: kv (move-in cash needed: deposit, first month, furniture basics, fees where legal; shortfall vs saved; months to save it; rent as a share of take-home); table (Cost | One-off | Monthly | Notes) including the things first-timers forget (contents insurance, broadband setup, a bed); a callout with the affordability rule of thumb and a verdict for this case; a checklist for viewing and signing safely.

tools.title: Compare job offers
tools.subtitle: Salary is not the whole number

inputs.label: The offers
inputs.placeholder: A: 30k, 5% pension match, hybrid, 25 days. B: 33k, no match, fully office, 20 days, 1h commute

tools.prompt: Offers: {offers}, home location from the profile. Sections: table (Factor | Offer A | Offer B | Annual value estimate) covering pay, pension match, commute cost and time, holiday, bonuses, training; kv (total compensation estimate for each, monthly net after commute for each, the tie-breaker question); a quote with a polite negotiation message to the lower offer; a callout on what to verify in the contract before accepting.

tools.title: My first 12 months
tools.subtitle: Milestones from payday one
tools.prompt: Build a 12-month money plan for the profile's first year on this salary. Sections: table (Month | Milestone | Amount | Why now) covering buffer, pension check, credit basics, tax-code check, first pay review; checklist for the first 30 days (payslip check, tax code, pension enrolment, bank account setup, automatic transfers); a callout on the annual tax and pay-review moments to put in the diary; a quote with a one-sentence rule to remember every payday.

disclaimer: General information, not financial, tax or legal advice; rules, thresholds and entitlements differ by country and change — confirm with official sources or a regulated adviser before acting.
